jobs.title: Treasury Lead
jobs.location: London or remote within the UK
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

Our vision is that our Finance team plays a central part of the business, somewhere the Board can rely on to support strategic planning. In this our treasury team keeps us safely funded and liquid and gives the Board and ALCO numbers they can trust. As we add products and markets, the team is growing. As second hire to the team, you’ll report directly to our Treasurer, sitting at the heart of how we capture, report, analyse and manage risk to support how we optimise Griffin’s balance sheet.

The opportunity

Treasury at a fintech bank is different. You’ll see real-time payment flows and deposit behaviour that a conventional bank never sees. You’ll work directly with our Treasurer to build our treasury processes, reporting and systems rather than inherit them. You’ll contribute to management of liquidity as a Direct FPS participant, use of facilities within the Bank of England’s Sterling Monetary Framework (SMF), card issuing and stablecoin infrastructure.

What success looks like

By month 3, you’ll understand our business and processes, run daily reporting with Michael’s review and handle daily cash positioning, including our Bank of England reserve account. By month 6, you’ll own daily and monthly reporting and run intraday cash management independently, including testing the SMF. You’ll have drafted ALCO papers and credit reviews, delivered your first automation improvements and contributed to the impact assessment for Direct FPS or a similar product launch.

To do this you’ll own

  • Daily and intraday reporting on liquidity, capital, interest rate risk, funding capacity and asset encumbrance, with every output sense-checked before it goes out

  • Risk monitoring against our risk appetite: limits, triggers and early warning indicators, forecast-versus-actual reviews, and stress tests you design with the Treasurer

  • Intraday cash management and liquidity forecasting: cash positioning, payments and transfers, depositor behaviour and outflow assumptions

  • Monthly management reporting, including interest income, margin and customer profitability, the ALCO pack, inputs to regulatory returns, and contributions to the ILAAP and ICAAP

  • Dealing operations: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations, settlements and collateral movements, plus credit analysis on counterparties and issuers. You’ll also cover for the Treasurer with brokers, treasury bill auctions and SMF drawdowns

  • Automating manual steps, closing control gaps, and documenting procedures that mean knowledge never sits with just two people

  • Maintaining our treasury bank and broker mandates

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To succeed in the role, we're looking for people who have:

  • 5+ years in a bank treasury function (e.g. middle-office, ALM or balance sheet management), measuring and reporting liquidity and capital from economic and regulatory perspectives. You will have produced reports hands-on rather than reviewed them

  • Strong prudential knowledge across liquidity, capital and leverage (e.g. CRR, Basel III, LCR, NSFR, IRRBB, ILAAP, ICAAP), and hands-on exposure to the dealing lifecycle: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations and settlements

  • Advanced Excel skills (e.g. data tables, scenario analysis, VBA), plus the attention to detail and reconciliation discipline to sense-check everything you produce

  • An analytical, inquisitive mindset, with a habit of automating what’s manual

  • The organisation and drive to work autonomously, remotely and asynchronously, and the appetite for the breadth and ambiguity of building in an early-stage bank

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write )

Ideally, you would also:

  • Hold a treasury or accountancy qualification (ACT, CertBALM, FRM, CFA, ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

  • Bring Python, SQL, Power BI or AI skills

  • Knowledge of Direct FPS and Bank of England SMF facilities

  • Experience implementing or using treasury or ALM systems

What can we offer you?

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

Learn more about our culture.

The team

You'll join our Operational Controls team within the Service guild, working across all operations functions. This team is the backbone of how Griffin stays compliant and keeps operational risk visible and manageable as we scale.

The opportunity

We're looking for someone to become the person who tells us, with confidence, whether our operations are actually working the way we think they are. You'll build and run our first-line controls programme from the ground up, working across deeply technical specialists and senior stakeholders alike. As Griffin scales, our control framework has to scale with it. You'll be central to making that happen, turning quality controls and assurance into a genuine source of confidence for the business.

What success looks like

In your first year, you'll have built meaningful relationships across every corner of Griffin, from operations teams to second line risk and compliance. You'll have helped stand up our controls capabilities from scratch, and you'll have taken full ownership of the RCSA process for the Service guild. Along the way, you'll have developed the QA/QC testing frameworks and MI that help leadership see exactly where our controls are strong and where they need attention.

To do this you'll own

  • Quality assurance reviews and quality control testing across operations, ensuring processes are executed accurately and in line with approved procedures

  • Sample-based testing and control checks, identifying errors, control gaps, exceptions, and potential operational risks

  • Corrective action and remediation plans, working with operations teams to close out issues within agreed timelines

  • The Service guild controls attestation framework, and support risk owners in first-line RCSA exercises

  • QA/QC testing frameworks, control checklists, sampling methodologies, and quality standards

  • Regular QA/QC reporting and MI, feeding into Griffin-wide operational risk reporting

  • Coordination of internal audit, external audit, compliance, risk, and regulatory reviews, providing evidence of operational controls and remediation

We expect you to shape this role:

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves,that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

We're looking for people who have:

  • Strong experience in Operations QA/QC, control testing, transaction testing, or operational risk management within a bank or financial institution

  • Experience reviewing operational processes and identifying errors, exceptions, control weaknesses, and process gaps

  • Experience making recommendations to strengthen controls.

  • Strong analytical and MI/data analysis skills, with experience producing QA/QC reports, dashboards, and trend analysis

  • The ability to challenge Operations constructively and operate with an independent control mindset

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

What can we offer you?

  • Salary: £50-60k (DOE)

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

Infrastructure sits within the Craft function. We’re a small team of three - two engineers and an engineering manager - who work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner. It’s our job to build the foundations that everything else at Griffin runs on: the systems, the tooling, the automation that helps us run a highly resilient and reliable platform and lets other teams ship fast. We're a software engineering team as much as an infrastructure team: we write the code that runs our platform, not just the configuration around it.

When we start work, we explore multiple solutions before picking one. We write RFCs, build proof-of-concepts, and run experiments to validate approaches. Once we commit to building something, we care about maintainability more than cleverness, observability more than hoping it works, and scalability over premature optimisation. We take the necessary time to ship quality solutions rather than hitting arbitrary deadlines. Once something goes live, we refactor the rough edges rather than polish what's already working.

The opportunity

Day to day, you'll build and manage the infrastructure the bank runs on - both in the cloud and on our own hardware in third party data centres. This means running FoundationDB clusters and writing the software and tooling for hitless upgrades, managing Kubernetes, writing infrastructure as code in Pulumi and CDK, running the Bazel build farm, and owning the deployment pipeline from CI to production.

Operational resilience is a big part of the job: replica clusters, multi-region failover, and chaos engineering to test how systems handle failures. Security access, CircleCI pipelines, DataDog integration, and cloud spend all fall under infrastructure too.

On our roadmap currently is: building out our self-hosted infrastructure to support a hybrid-cloud setup and remove single-vendor reliance, improving how Kubernetes scales, improving the build farm, and building out our PKI infrastructure. We also have plans for a global HTTP routing layer to allow seamless failover between sites. Much of this is software we built ourselves, and you'll shape it from the first design through to production.

Our infrastructure as code is written in TypeScript. Where it makes sense, tooling gets written in Clojure. There's some Rust too.

What success looks like

Infrastructure problems become production problems fast. Success here means thinking ahead - identifying issues with scale, security, or compliance before they affect services.

You've eliminated an entire class of incidents by fixing the underlying architectural issue. You've proven the database and compute platform can handle 10x current traffic volumes by working with backend teams to stress-test it. You've cut deploy times in half by rethinking how the pipeline works. You've tested multi-region failover under realistic failure scenarios and it worked.

You've shipped well-tested software that turns risky manual operations, like database upgrades, into routine, hitless ones that the whole team maintains with confidence.

You've redesigned service discovery to remove networking issues that used to cause weekly firefights. When new FCA requirements dropped, you were already compliant because you'd built the infrastructure to handle it months earlier.

To do this, you'll own

  • Infrastructure architecture decisions - how we structure our systems, what approaches we take, what tools we build

  • Production reliability - keeping the database, compute, build farm, and deployment pipelines running and improving them

  • What other teams depend on to ship - CI/CD, security access, monitoring integration, and the infrastructure that lets engineers deploy safely

  • Infrastructure cost and efficiency - managing spend and resource usage across AWS and DataDog

  • Infrastructure software - the code behind our database control plane, operational tooling and automation, from design and implementation through to testing, code review and maintenance

Stack: FoundationDB, Kubernetes, Bazel, Pulumi, CDK, CircleCI, DataDog, Clojure, TypeScript

Your background

You'll fit in well here if you have:

  • Solid systems experience - you've run container orchestration in production, written infrastructure as code, and understand IP networking well enough to debug it when things go wrong

  • Cloud infrastructure experience - you've built and managed production environments, worked with networking, identity management, and compute at scale

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals - you write code to solve problems, and you're as comfortable designing, testing and reviewing production software as you are configuring infrastructure. TypeScript, Python, Go, or functional languages are all fine. If your experience only extends to Bash scripting and YAML, we probably aren't a good fit for you

  • Comfort with startup environments - small teams, shifting priorities, high autonomy

We write a lot of our tooling in Clojure - our database control plane, operational scripts, and automation. You don't need Clojure experience coming in, but you'll need to learn it once you're here. If you've worked with functional languages before, that helps.

Regardless, you should be comfortable picking up new languages and approaches as we do find ourselves reading through the codebases of open-source systems and tools we use to understand their behaviour, and they are written in a diverse range of languages we don't use ourselves.

What can we offer you?

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and product. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them, keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in:

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time)

  • Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

  • Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

  • Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

  • Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

  • Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

  • Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

  • Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

  • Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed)

Being our DPO means:

  • advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

  • monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

  • training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

  • being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

  • Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.

  • Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products, like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.

  • Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams.

  • An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required.

  • A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.

  • The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

  • A love of writing. We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write).

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.

  • Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.

  • Have worked in finance or banking.

What can we offer you?

  • Salary: £ 80-100k (DOE)

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin

  • Step 3: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in other teams for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance
